name: Enza Cafe
short_description: Popular cafe directly at the Snow Monkey Park trailhead, serving ramen, pizza, apple pie, soft serve, and the iconic Monkey Marshmallow Latte.
long_description: Enza Cafe is the go-to warm-up stop before and after visiting Jigokudani Snow Monkey Park. Situated right in front of the trail entrance, it serves a crowd-pleasing menu of ramen (excellent for warming up on cold days), thin-crust pizza with Nagano mushroom toppings, fried chicken, apple hand pies, Shinshu apple soft serve ice cream, and the wildly popular Monkey Marshmallow Latte (hot latte topped with a monkey-shaped marshmallow). Seating is both indoor and outdoor. Winter hours are extended (8:30am) for early-bird monkey watchers and skiers.
signature_dishes: Shinshu apple soft serve ice cream
notes: Located 35km / 50 min from central Nagano City. Access: take bus from Yudanaka Station to Snow Monkey Park bus stop. Open daily, all seasons. Ski season (Dec-Mar) extended morning hours are key for skiers who also want to see Snow Monkeys. Average spend: ¥1,000-1,999.

name: Yudanaka Brewery Complex U
name_local: ゆダナカ ブルワリーコンプレックスU
short_description: Contemporary craft brewery and restaurant using Shinshu ingredients and Yudanaka hot spring water, with QR-code ordering in English.
long_description: Opened in 2022, Yudanaka Brewery Complex U is the most modern food-and-drink destination in the Yudanaka area. The brewery produces original craft beers using local Nagano ingredients and water from Yudanaka's natural springs. The restaurant serves carefully curated Shinshu-focused dishes alongside the house beers. The entire complex is housed in a striking building with ample parking (30 spaces). QR-code menu ordering is available in English — a significant practical advantage. The complex also houses a 2nd-floor day-trip onsen bath facility. A hit with both day-trippers from Nagano City and onsen town visitors looking for something non-traditional.
notes: Closes at 6pm — arrive early. The only establishment in Yudanaka area with QR-code English ordering. Has 30 parking spaces. Also has 2nd-floor day-trip onsen (open same hours). Tabelog listing: https://tabelog.com/en/nagano/A2001/A200104/20026081/

name: Hakko Yamanouchi
short_description: Fermentation-focused dining bar with local craft beers, sake, and creative Shinshu-ingredient small plates — one of the best dining experiences near Yudanaka Station.
long_description: Hakko Yamanouchi (発酵 = fermentation) is a beloved local bar/restaurant that celebrates Nagano's fermentation culture — from miso to sake to pickles. The menu features inventive small plates such as smoked pickles with gorgonzola, ginger-roasted chicken, and vegan-friendly tofu-mushroom dishes alongside an excellent selection of local craft beers, sake, and house cocktails. Staff are friendly and the English menu makes ordering accessible for international visitors. Closed Mondays. Particularly warm in winter when the après-ski crowd fills the cosy wooden interior.
notes: #4 restaurant in Yamanouchi-machi on TripAdvisor (68 reviews, 4.6/5). Located 5 min walk from Yudanaka Station along Kaede Street. Staff speak limited English but menu has English translations. Stays open until 11pm, making it one of the later-closing options in town.

name: Japanese Dining GOEN
name_local: ジャパニーズダイニング 御苑
short_description: Casual Japanese restaurant directly opposite Yudanaka Station, serving sashimi, tempura, karaage, soba ramen, and sushi — with vegan options.
long_description: GOEN (御苑) blends modern design with traditional Japanese service in its prime location directly across from Yudanaka Station. It serves a wide-ranging menu of Japanese dishes including tempura, sashimi, karaage (fried chicken), omakase sushi rolls, and a distinctive 'soba ramen' fusion dish. The restaurant also serves Western-style food, desserts, and coffee, making it reliably versatile. Available vegan sushi options and some English-speaking staff. Good for families and groups with mixed dietary preferences. Has both ground-floor hall seating and a 2nd-floor dining area with terrace.
notes: Hours may vary significantly by season — call or check Google Maps before visiting. Has vegan sushi options (explicitly mentioned by reviewer). Located 27 meters from Yudanaka Station. Catering and banquet services available. Bilingual menu makes ordering easy.

name: Isami Zushi
short_description: Family-run sushi restaurant steps from Yudanaka Station, praised for fresh sashimi and generous portions — open until 11pm.
long_description: Isami Zushi (いさみ寿司) is a popular neighbourhood sushi restaurant located 185 metres from Yudanaka Station, run by a welcoming older Japanese couple known for their hospitality toward foreign visitors. The menu features fresh nigiri, sashimi, and rolls at reasonable prices. The grilled yellowtail fish head is a standout dish. Open until 11pm — one of the later-closing restaurants in Yudanaka. Vegetarian guests can order tamago (egg) sushi and cucumber rolls. The warm, intimate atmosphere and accommodating hosts make it a favourite for repeat visitors to the area.
notes: TripAdvisor 4.7/5 from 36 reviews — one of the highest-rated restaurants in Yamanouchi. Phone: 0269-33-2311. Located 185m from Yudanaka Station. Vegetarian: tamago and cucumber rolls available. Cash only — bring yen. Hours consistent across all days per TripAdvisor.

name: Izakaya Kushidoraku
short_description: Authentic Japanese yakitori and barbecue izakaya with picture English menu, cosy tatami seating, and some of the best gyoza in Yudanaka.
long_description: Kushidoraku (串道楽 — 'skewer pleasure') is an old-school, wood-interior izakaya near the station that attracts a loyal local crowd and adventurous international visitors. The menu covers yakitori skewers (including unusual options like chicken cartilage, hearts, and wings), gyoza dumplings (celebrated as some of the best in Yudanaka), miso soup, potato croquettes, and various grilled meats. An English picture menu makes ordering accessible. Tatami floor seating with low tables creates an authentic Japanese dining atmosphere. The owner and staff can communicate basic English and have a warm approach to international guests. Staff are flexible with vegetarian requests (will cook dishes without fish).
notes: Reserve in advance especially in peak season (Jan-Mar). TripAdvisor #22 of 153 Yamanouchi restaurants. Open very late (midnight) — one of the few options for late-night dining. Smoking permitted inside (check current ventilation). The owner can occasionally be brusque on busy nights — persevere. Staff said to cook vegetarian dishes without fish when asked.

name: Asashinaya Shokudo
short_description: Friendly family-run shokudo (casual diner) serving a broad Japanese menu including ramen, soba, tempura, tonkatsu and gyoza — with English picture menu.
long_description: Asashinaya Shokudo is the classic neighbourhood Japanese diner (食堂 = shokudo) in Yudanaka. The menu covers all the bases: ramen (¥700-800), soba, tonkatsu (pork cutlet), tempura, karaage, udon, and curry — classic everyday Japanese fare. The owner-operator is consistently praised for warmth and efficiency. An English picture menu with photos and descriptions makes ordering easy. Particularly popular for families and groups with mixed tastes. Ramen and gyoza are highlights. Located a 10-15 minute walk from Yudanaka Station with roadside parking. The owner sometimes gives out small souvenirs to guests on departure.
notes: Hours not listed online — call ahead or check Google Maps. Located ~10-15 min walk from Yudanaka Station. Has parking. Vegetarian: tempura tofu-miso broth dish available when requested. Has been serving the Yudanaka area for many years. TripAdvisor #21 of 153 (4.3/5). Recommended by multiple local ryokan owners to guests.

name: Soba Dokoro Yariya
short_description: Casual soba house near Yudanaka with cold and hot Shinshu buckwheat noodles, horse meat sashimi (basashi), and housemade karaage — open until 11pm, cash only.
long_description: Sobadokoro Yariya is a straightforward, affordable soba restaurant in the Yudanaka area serving classic Shinshu-style buckwheat noodles, both cold (zaru soba) and hot (kake soba). The menu also extends to karaage (fried chicken), fresh apple with each meal, and roast soba tea. For adventurous visitors, basashi (horse meat sashimi) is available — a Nagano specialty. All meals are accompanied by a fresh Shinshu apple. The restaurant is cash-only and does not accept any electronic payments. Open until 11pm daily which is later than most Yudanaka establishments.
notes: Cash only — no card, no electronic money, no QR code. Average spend under ¥999. Located 1.6km from Yudanaka Station (20 min walk or short drive). Hours per Tabelog: 11:00-23:00 daily. All meals served with fresh apple and roast soba tea. Roast soba tea for purchase to take home.

name: Chanko Tamaya
name_local: ちゃんこ料理 たまや
short_description: Sumo-themed restaurant steps from Yudanaka Station, specialising in chanko-nabe (sumo stew) with yakitori and grilled meats.
long_description: Chanko Tamaya is a fun, thematic dining experience — a sumo-themed restaurant decorated with sumo photographs and artifacts, located just 2 minutes on foot from Yudanaka Station. The signature dish is chanko-nabe (ちゃんこ鍋), the highly nutritious stew traditionally served at sumo stables that includes chicken, vegetables, tofu, and other ingredients in a rich broth. The menu also includes yakitori, minced crab dumplings, and grilled pork. Capacity of 35 seats (30 floor seating, 5 chairs). No reservations required. Closed Wednesdays.
notes: 2 min walk from Yudanaka Station main exit. Closed Wednesdays and Dec 31/Jan 1. Average spend ¥2,000-3,000. Dinner only (evenings). Sumo-themed decor is a fun novelty. Cash only likely — confirm at time of visit.

name: D-Line Kitchen & Bar
short_description: Quirky retro pub/cafe 1 minute from Yudanaka Station with pizza, cocktails, Japanese whisky, and late-night après-ski atmosphere.
long_description: D-Line is a retro-vibed bar-cafe in a distinctive building right next to Yudanaka Station. Known for an eclectic interior aesthetic, excellent Japanese whisky selection (including premium Scotch and domestic labels), cocktails, and simple food including pizza. Open from 6pm nightly, it's the closest thing Yudanaka has to a dedicated après-ski bar. Popular with international visitors and ski-season workers. The pizza is consistently praised. Closed Thursdays.
notes: 87 metres from Yudanaka Station. Closed Thursdays. Evening only. One of the very few places in Yudanaka open past 10pm. Japanese whisky selection is notably good — ask the bartender for recommendations. Retro 'Shining'-esque decor has cult following.

name: Sekiei Drive-In
short_description: Old-school Japanese drive-in diner near Yudanaka with lunch and dinner service — a local institution since 1967.
long_description: Sekiei Drive-In is a local legend — a classic Japanese cafeteria-style diner that has been serving Yudanaka since its opening on March 5, 1967. The menu covers standard Japanese comfort food. The drive-in format and large portions make it popular with families and groups. Limited to lunch and dinner service (closed Sundays and Mondays based on current schedule). An 8-minute walk from Yudanaka Station. Expect Japanese-language menus and minimal English service.
notes: Opened 1967. Closed Sun-Mon. Last order 20:00 (8pm) — closes early. Cash only. 8 min walk from Yudanaka Station (461m). Limited English — pointing at menu or translating photos recommended.

name: Ichidaya
short_description: Cosy local izakaya with yakitori, shishamo, grilled squid, and a welcoming neighbourhood atmosphere.
long_description: Ichidaya is an intimate local izakaya near Yudanaka Station known for its simple, honest grilled food and neighbourhood charm. The menu focuses on yakitori (chicken skewers), shishamo (smelt fish), grilled squid, and other classic izakaya staples. The small space and tatami seating create a genuinely local feeling, making it popular with ski and snowboard workers as well as Japanese guests. Limited English.
notes: TripAdvisor rated 4.6/5 (12 reviews). Cosy local gem. Limited hours — call ahead. Cash only. Primarily Japanese-speaking — bring a translation app. Reservations recommended in peak season.

name: Shimaya Soba
short_description: Traditional Shinshu soba restaurant connected with Shimaya ryokan, serving handmade buckwheat noodles with local Nagano sides.
long_description: Shimaya Soba is the dining operation associated with Shimaya Ryokan in central Yudanaka, specialising in handmade Shinshu soba (信州そば). Shinshu-style soba uses locally grown buckwheat and is typically served cold (zaru) or hot. Accompaniments include nozawana pickles, tofu, and seasonal mountain vegetables. The soba is made fresh daily from high-quality buckwheat flour. Note that this is a separate establishment from the ryokan's room accommodation — the restaurant is open to non-guests.
signature_dishes: Zaru soba (cold handmade Shinshu buckwheat noodles)
notes: Part of Shimaya Ryokan complex. Open to non-guests. Hours vary — contact via ryokan website or by phone. Cash only. Soba is made fresh daily in limited quantities — go early to avoid sell-out.

name: Dohshokan
short_description: Traditional Japanese restaurant in Yudanaka offering local Shinshu cuisine including soba, seasonal mountain vegetables, and river fish.
long_description: Dohshokan (道松館) is a local traditional Japanese restaurant in Yudanaka Onsen that serves classic Shinshu regional cuisine. The menu centres on locally foraged mountain vegetables (sansai), Chikuma river fish, handmade soba, and other Nagano staples. The atmosphere is traditional and unhurried — a good representation of rural Japanese dining culture. Limited English, but the proprietors are welcoming to international guests who make the effort to visit.
notes: Data is limited — confirm hours by phone or in person before visiting. Cash only expected. A genuine local establishment, not tourism-facing. Best visited with some Japanese language capability or a translation app.

name: Tamagawa Soba (Shibu Onsen)
name_local: 手打ちそば うどん 玉川
short_description: Handmade soba and udon restaurant in Shibu Onsen with three signature styles: zaru, tororo, and kurumidare (walnut sauce soba) — only daily-made quantities available.
long_description: Tamagawa is a long-standing handmade soba restaurant in the quaint Shibu Onsen village, about 1km uphill from Yudanaka. Each morning the family prepares by hand only enough soba for the day — once it's sold out, they close. Signature items are zaru soba (plain cold noodles), tororo soba (with grated mountain yam), and kurumidare soba (with walnut sauce, a Nagano regional specialty). The soba soft serve ice cream is only available to guests who order noodles. Limited seating. Smoking prohibited.
signature_dishes: Soba soft serve ice cream (with soba order only)
notes: Located in Shibu Onsen — 20 min walk uphill from Yudanaka Station (or short taxi/bus ride). Closes when daily soba supply runs out — arrive early at lunch. No smoking. Soba soft serve only for soba-ordering customers. Vegetarian-friendly as soba broth can be made without fish stock on request.

name: Snow Monkey Beer Live
name_local: スノーモンキービアライブ
short_description: Annual craft beer and live music festival on the Shiga Kogen ski slopes in mid-March — a bucket-list après-ski event.
long_description: Snow Monkey Beer Live is an annual craft beer festival held on the slopes of Shiga Kogen in mid-March, combining Japanese microbrewery beers with live music performances. The event celebrates the end of ski season with a festival atmosphere on the mountain, and typically draws visitors from across Japan and internationally. Tickets and timing vary year-to-year — check the official website for current season dates. The event is a highlight of the Japanese ski social calendar.
notes: Annual event — mid-March typically. Check http://snowmonkey.jp/ for current year dates and ticket booking. Held at Shiga Kogen ski resort (not Yudanaka town itself, but a major regional event). Times vary by day. A must-attend for ski/craft beer enthusiasts.

name: Chinese Food Eiraku
short_description: Long-standing Chinese-Japanese restaurant near Yudanaka offering ramen, gyoza, and Japanese-Chinese comfort food at very low prices.
long_description: Eiraku (永楽 — 'eternal prosperity') is a no-frills Chinese-Japanese restaurant that has served the Yudanaka community for decades. The menu features classic Japanese Chinese-style food: ramen, gyoza, fried rice, and Chinese-influenced set meals. Counter seating with a local, unpretentious atmosphere. Widely recommended for its small ramen and gyoza combo — very filling and very cheap. The language barrier is real, but pointing at simple menu items works fine.
notes: Very cheap and filling — ideal for budget travellers. Counter seating, very local. Hours unknown — check Google Maps before going. Cash only. No English menu.

name: Tofuya
short_description: Traditional tofu-focused restaurant in Yudanaka serving fresh handmade Shinshu tofu dishes and local seasonal accompaniments.
long_description: Tofuya (豆腐屋 — 'tofu shop/restaurant') is a traditional establishment in Yudanaka area that specialises in handmade Shinshu-style tofu (豆腐), including hiyayakko (cold fresh tofu), agedashi dofu (deep-fried tofu in broth), yudofu (hot pot tofu), and dengaku tofu (grilled tofu with miso). Shinshu tofu is noted for its richness owing to the quality of regional mountain water and locally grown soybeans. The restaurant's dishes are simple, wholesome, and represent an important vein of Nagano traditional cuisine. Vegetarian-friendly relative to most local options.
notes: Note: Tofuya in Yudanaka is NOT the same as the famous 'Tofuya Ukai' luxury chain in Tokyo/Kawasaki. This is a small local Yudanaka tofu restaurant. Hours and specific address unconfirmed — verify directly. Tofu broth may contain fish-based dashi — ask if vegetarian.

name: Lawson (Yudanaka Ekimae)
name_local: ローソン 湯田中駅前店
short_description: Essential convenience store (konbini) 87 metres from Yudanaka Station — onigiri, bento, hot foods, ATM (accepts foreign cards), ski essentials.
long_description: The Lawson convenience store at Yudanaka Station is an essential stop for all travellers in the area. For skiers, it is the place to grab breakfast before the mountain bus, quick lunches, energy bars, hot coffee, nikuman (steamed meat buns), onigiri (rice balls), and snacks. The ATM inside accepts international cards (VISA/Mastercard) — critical in this largely cash-based town. Open hours may vary from the standard 24-hour format for rural locations. Stock also includes sandwiches, bento boxes, noodle cups, desserts, sauces, and basic toiletries. Children's snacks and drinks available.
notes: 87m from Yudanaka Station. ATM accepts international Visa/Mastercard — important for cash in this area. Not confirmed 24-hour in this rural location — check hours on Google Maps before counting on late-night access. Take-out only format. Tabelog category: Convenience store.

name: 7-Eleven Yamanouchi Sano
name_local: セブン-イレブン 山ノ内町佐野店
short_description: The 7-Eleven on Route 292 in Sano — critical konbini for drivers headed to Snow Monkey Park, Ryuoo ski area, or Shiga Kogen.
long_description: The 7-Eleven in the Sano district of Yamanouchi is situated on Route 292 (Joshinetsu Expressway spur), making it the primary convenience store for travellers driving toward Snow Monkey Park, Ryuoo Ski Area, or Shiga Kogen. Stock includes standard konbini fare: hot foods, coffee, onigiri, sandwiches, snacks, drinks, basic medicines, and convenience items. ATM service available (may accept international cards). Hotarutei Villas notes this store as 5 minutes by car from their property.
notes: 722m from Yudanaka Station. On Route 292 — key stop for drivers. Hours likely not 24hr in this rural area — check Google Maps. Important for Hotarutei Villas guests (5 min drive). The nearest 7-Eleven for many Kanbayashi-area accommodations.

name: Tsuruya Supermarket (Nakano / Yamanouchi Branch)
short_description: Nagano's beloved regional supermarket chain with outstanding local produce — Shinshu apples, miso, soba, nozawana, sake, and the famous Tsuruya original products.
long_description: Tsuruya is the premium supermarket chain of Nagano Prefecture, beloved by both locals and savvy visitors for its exceptional selection of local Shinshu products, fresh produce, and prepared foods. A Tsuruya stop is a highlight for food-curious travellers: look for Shinshu apples in season (September-November), locally milled soba flour, hand-fermented miso, nozawana pickles, walnut sauce, local sake, and the chain's own excellent prepared foods and bakery products. The nearest large Tsuruya branches are in Nakano City or Yamanouchi area — approximately 15-20 minutes' drive from central Yudanaka. The Ippongi Park area has a branch.
address: Nakano City / Yamanouchi area, Nagano (multiple branches)
notes: Hotarutei Villas staff recommend Tsuruya Ippongi (10 min by car) or AEON Nakano (10 min by car) for full grocery shopping. Tsuruya own-brand products make excellent souvenirs — particularly the apple products and soba. Accepts cards at most branches. Hours approximately 9am-9pm.

name: Mikasa
short_description: Small local cafe in Yudanaka serving coffee, tea, light meals and desserts.
long_description: Mikasa is a small neighbourhood cafe near Yudanaka Station, serving standard Japanese cafe fare — coffee, tea, soft drinks, light meals, and desserts. A quiet spot to warm up between activities. Limited English but standard pointing-at-menu service works. Cash likely expected.
notes: Limited data available. Primarily a local hangout. Best for coffee and light snacks rather than a full meal. Verify hours before visiting.

name: Ryokan Kaiseki Dining (In-House)
short_description: The highest-quality dining in Yudanaka happens inside ryokan dining rooms — kaiseki multi-course meals featuring Shinshu beef, river fish, sansai, and local seasonal produce.
long_description: For serious food experiences in Yudanaka, the in-house kaiseki (懐石) dinners at the premium ryokan — particularly Yorozuya, Kambayashi Hotel Senjukaku, Hotel Issa-tei/Biyu no Yado, Tawaraya, and Aburaya Tousen — represent the pinnacle of local Shinshu cuisine. A typical winter kaiseki at these properties includes: sakizuke (small starter), hassun (seasonal platter), yakimono (grilled Shinshu beef or river fish), mushimono (steamed dish), simmered mountain vegetables, rice with local pickles (nozawana, shinshuu miso), miso soup, and dessert (often apple compote or matcha sweet). Most are served in private dining rooms or at low traditional tables. Reservations are part of the booking process for ryokan stays; some accept outside guests for dinner (call ahead).
signature_dishes: River fish (iwana, yamame — Chikuma River trout/char)
Sansai (wild mountain vegetables — fiddleheads, butterbur, etc.)
notes: This is a category entry for the in-house ryokan dining experience. Top ryokan for kaiseki: Yorozuya ($$$$), Kambayashi Senjukaku ($$$$), Biyu no Yado ($$$), Tawaraya ($$$). Most accommodate dietary restrictions with 24hr advance notice. Some properties (Senjukaku) accept non-guests for dinner — call ahead. Kaiseki at these properties is ¥5,000-15,000/person typically.

name: Chokkun
short_description: Local izakaya-dining bar with ramen, draft beer, and izakaya fare — QR payment accepted.
long_description: Chokkun is a local neighbourhood izakaya and dining bar that spans several categories — izakaya, dining bar, and ramen. It's a laid-back spot for local workers and the occasional international visitor looking for inexpensive Japanese food and drinks. Notably, it accepts QR code payments (PayPay etc.) but not credit cards — useful for visitors with Japanese payment apps.
notes: 1.8km from Yudanaka Station (20 min walk). Accepts QR code payments (PayPay), but not credit cards. Average spend ¥1,500. Hours and closing days not confirmed — verify before visiting.

name: Oyaki and Shinshu Street Food (Various Vendors)
name_local: おやき・信州郷土料理
short_description: Look for oyaki (stuffed buckwheat dumplings), Shinshu apple products, and local food vendors in and around Yudanaka and on the Snow Monkey Park trail.
long_description: Oyaki (おやき) are a defining Nagano street food — dough parcels (from wheat, buckwheat, or millet) stuffed with fillings including nozawana (pickled greens), kabocha squash, red bean paste, eggplant miso, or mushroom. They are steamed or baked and served warm. Look for oyaki at Enza Cafe (near Snow Monkey Park), at the Tsuruya supermarket, and occasionally at small stalls in the Yudanaka/Shibu Onsen area. Shinshu apple products — fresh juice, apple pie, apple soft serve, and apple jam — are available at Enza Cafe and various convenience stores. These foods represent the most accessible and affordable local Nagano specialties.
address: Various locations — Yudanaka, Shibu Onsen, Snow Monkey Park trail
notes: Best oyaki at Enza Cafe (buckwheat buns), Tsuruya supermarket, and roadside stalls. Nozawana and vegetable fillings are vegetarian. Red bean filling is vegan. Ask about dashi in broth-based dishes. Apple products are best in autumn (Sep-Nov) but available year-round as processed goods.
